content: 1. Metronidazole can inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 2. Metronidazole may increase the levels or effects of piroxicam by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, but its significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 3. Polycarbophil can reduce tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Polysaccharide iron can decrease tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Tetracycline and porfimer may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to enhanced photosensitivity. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Metronidazole may increase prednisone levels or effects by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Primidone can decrease tetracycline levels or effects by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Metronidazole may increase propafenone levels or effects by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 9. Bismuth subsalicylate and propranolol may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing severe hypertension due to renal prostaglandin synthesis blockage. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Metronidazole and propylene glycol may interact by decreasing metabolism, leading to a disulfiram-like reaction. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Tetracycline may increase the effects of protamine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 12. Tetracycline may decrease pyridoxine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance is unknown. 13. Metronidazole may also decrease pyridoxine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance is unknown. 14.
